answer: When k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, the escrow penalty counts implicated identity pairs, so aggregate liability grows as O(k²), not merely with the number of signatures. A detected swarm also faces an exponential capital-loss multiplier through compounded slashing and asymmetric depreciation, making cheap identity splitting costly. A jetty, willow, and glacier may be distinct, but shared control links their risk.
